sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-464.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 464 was established by Ordinance No. 22988, passed by the Dallas City Council on January 8, 1997. Ordinance No. 22988 amended Ordinance Nos. 10962 and 19455, Chapters 51 and 51A of the Dallas City Code, as amended. Ordinance No. 22988 was amended by Ordinance No. 23729, passed by the Dallas City Council on December 9, 1998. (Ord. Nos. 10962; 19455; 22988; 23729; 26042)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-464.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 464 is established on property generally bounded by Wheatland Road, Westmoreland Road, Kirnwood Drive, and Bolton Boone Drive. The size of PD 464 is approximately 45.722 acres. (Ord. Nos. 22988; 26042)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-464.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations contained in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In the event of a conflict, this article controls.

(b) In this article, MEDICAL OFFICE FACILITY means a facility, other than a hospital, for the examining, consulting with, and treatment of patients with medical, dental, or optical problems on an out-patient basis.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article refer to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A. In the event of a conflict, this article controls.

(d) For purposes of determining the applicability of regulations in this article and in Chapter 51A triggered by adjacency or proximity to another zoning district, and for purposes of interpreting the DIR and RAR requirements of Division 51A-4.800, this district is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. Nos. 22988; 26042)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-464.104. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

Except as provided in Section 51P-464.113, development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit 464A). In the event of a conflict between the provisions of this article and the development plan, the provisions of this article control. (Ord. Nos. 22988; 23729; 26042)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-464.105. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Agricultural uses.

-- None permitted.

(b) Commercial and business service uses.

-- Electronics service center. [L] -- Medical or scientific laboratory. [L] -- Commercial cleaning or laundry plant. [L] -- Custom business services. [L]

(c) Industrial uses.

-- None permitted.

(d) Institutional and community service uses.

-- Adult day care facility. [L] -- Child-care facility. [L] -- Church. [L] -- Community service center. -- Convalescent and nursing homes, hospice care, and related institutions. -- Hospital. -- Public or private school. [SUP]

(e) Lodging uses.

-- Hotel or motel. [L]

(f) Miscellaneous uses.

-- Temporary construction or sales office.

(g) Office uses.

-- Financial institution without drive-in window. [L] -- Medical office facility. -- Office, limited to administrative space in conjunction with the operation of a hospital.

(h) Recreation uses.

-- Private recreation center, club, or area.

(i) Residential uses.

-- Group residential facility. [SUP required if spacing component of Section 51A- 4.209(3) is not met.] -- Retirement housing.

(j) Retail and personal service uses.

-- Ambulance service. [L] -- Commercial parking lot or garage. [L] -- General merchandise or food store 3,500 square feet or less. [L] -- General merchandise or food store greater than 3,500 square feet. [L] -- Restaurant without drive-in or drive-through service. [L]

-- Theater. [L]

(k) Transportation uses.

-- Helistop. [L] -- Private street or alley. -- Transit passenger shelter. -- Transit passenger station or transfer center.

(l) Utility and public service uses.

-- Electrical substation. -- Local utilities. -- Post office. -- Radio, television, or microwave tower. [SUP] -- Tower/antenna for cellular communication. [SUP]

(m) Wholesale, distribution, and storage uses.

-- None permitted. (Ord. Nos. 22988; 26042)

sections.title: Limited Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-464.106. LIMITED USES.

For purposes of this PD, Sections 51A-4.218(b) and 51A-4.218(c)(2) do not apply. (Ord. Nos. 22988; 26042)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-464.107. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations contained in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217.

(b) The following accessory uses are not permitted in this district:

-- Accessory pathological waste incinerator. -- Medical/infectious waste incinerator. (Ord. Nos. 22988; 26042)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-464.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(a) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 25 feet.

(b) Side and rear yard. Minimum side yard and rear yard is 10 feet.

(c) Density. No maximum dwelling unit density.

(d) Floor area. Maximum floor area permitted is 4,800,000 square feet.

(e) Height.

(1) Maximum structure height. Except as otherwise provided in Paragraph (e)(2) below, maximum structure height is 240 feet.

(2) Residential proximity slope. If any portion of a structure is over 26 feet in height, that portion of a structure may not be located above a residential proximity slope. Exception: Structures listed in Section 51A-4.408(a)(2) may project through the slope to a height not to exceed the maximum structure height, or 12 feet above the slope, whichever is less.

(f) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 60 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(g) Lot size. No minimum lot size.

(h) Stories. No maximum number of stories. (Ord. Nos. 22988; 26042)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-464.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Except as otherwise provided, consult the use regulations contained in Division 51A- 4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use. Consult the off-street parking and loading regulations (Divisions 51A-4.300 et seq.) for information regarding off-street parking and loading generally.

(b) The following limited uses must, at a minimum, provide off-street parking at a ratio equal to 25 percent of the code required off-street parking for that use:

(1) Financial institution without drive-in window.

(2) General merchandise or food store greater than 3,500 square feet.

(3) Hotel or motel.

(c) Except for those limited uses listed in Subsection (b) above, no off-street parking is required for limited uses in this district. No off-street parking is required for the office use. (Ord. Nos. 22988; 26042)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-464.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. Nos. 22988; 26042)

sections.title: Tree Preservation
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-464.111. TREE PRESERVATION.

The regulations contained in Division 51A-10.130, “Tree Preservation,” apply to this PD. (Ord. Nos. 22988; 26042)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-464.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) For purposes of this PD, an artificial lot is the land area that includes any new building footprint or new off-street parking area and a minimum of 15 feet around the building footprint or off- street parking area. The artificial lot does not require public street frontage. No artificial lot created on the Property may contain an aggregate land area which exceeds 50 percent of the total land area contained in the PD.

(b) A landscape plan for an artificial lot that meets the following requirements must be submitted to the building official with each application for a building permit for a structure on the Property or an application for an electrical permit in conjunction with the lighting of a surface parking area:

(1) Minimum six-foot-high solid screening for off-street loading areas must be provided to screen off-street loading areas from adjoining property lines and public streets and alleys. Screening must be composed of materials listed in Section 51A-4.602(b)(3).

(2) Site trees must be provided as follows:

(A) Within six months after final inspection of the first new structure on the Property but prior to the issuance of a final certificate of occupancy for a use within that structure, a minimum of 50 large canopy trees, each with a minimum caliper of three inches in size, must be planted a minimum of 50 feet on-center and located within 30 feet of the property lines along the Wheatland Road and Bolton Boone Drive frontages.

(B) Prior to the issuance of a building permit for any subsequent structures on the Property, a minimum of one large canopy tree with a minimum caliper of three inches in size is required for each 4,000 square feet of land area within a designated artificial lot, up to a maximum of 35 trees. These trees must be planted 50 feet on-center and within 30 feet of the property lines along Wheatland Road and Bolton Boone Drive.

(C) Upon compliance with Subparagraphs (2)(A) and (2)(B) above, the landscape plan submitted with each subsequently designated artificial lot must include one site tree, a minimum caliper of three inches in size, for each 4,000 square feet of land area. These site trees may be planted at any location on the Property.

(3) All surface parking spaces must be located within 120 feet from the trunk of a large canopy tree.

(4) A minimum of two design standards listed in Section 51A-10.126 must be incorporated into each landscape plan.

(c) When Westmoreland Avenue is improved south of Wheatland Road and the existing tree line located on the Property, as shown on the Tree Preservation Development Plan (Exhibit 464B), is removed, a minimum of 30 large canopy trees, each with a minimum caliper of three inches in size, must be planted a minimum of 50 feet on-center within 30 feet of the property line along Westmoreland Road. (Ord. Nos. 22988; 26042)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-464.113. SIGNS.

(a) Except as provided below, signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts contained in Article VII.

(b) Non-premise signs are prohibited on the Property.

(c) Movement control signs may have a maximum height of 20 feet and a maximum effective area (which does not include supports) of 50 square feet per side. These signs are not limited in number nor is there any required distance between these signs. Movement control signs must provide a minimum setback of five feet and must comply with the requirements of the visibility obstruction regulations contained in the Dallas Development Code.

(d) Except as provided in Subsection (e), detached premise signs may not exceed 200 square feet in effective area.

(e) For the seven signs identified on the development plan and listed on Attachment A (Exhibit 464C), the height and effective area of these signs must be as described on Attachment A, and the location must be as shown on the development plan.

(f) Additional signs, including movement control and premise signs, may be erected on the Property without amending the development plan. In no instance, however, may the number of premise signs exceed that number permitted under the provisions for business zoning district contained in Article VII. (Ord. Nos. 22988; 23729; 26042)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-464.114. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 22988; 26042)

sections.title: Zoning Map
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-464.115. ZONING MAP.

PD 464 is located on Zoning Map Nos. P-5 and Q-5. (Ord. Nos. 22988; 26042)
